The corresponding wet weight at birth is exceptionally low, estimated at roughly 0.0123 grams [Wwb = roughly 0.0123 grams], placing this species among the lighter livebearers within its family. This sexual dimorphism in both growth rate and maturation timing is a hallmark of poeciliid life histories, where males invest heavily in early reproduction while females prioritize further somatic expansion to enhance future fecundity. The slower female developmental pace is also reflected in the greater ultimate body size they achieve, a pattern consistent with the reproductive demands of carrying broods throughout gestation.
